original_question: If a complex polynomial P of degree n>1 shares at least one root with each of its derivatives P^(k) for k=1,...,n-1, must P be of the form b(z-a)^n for some complex numbers a and nonzero b?
target_in_paper: Section 7.3, Problem 30 (Casas-Alvero’s conjecture): the paper’s exact target is the complex Casas-Alvero conjecture for univariate polynomials, not a broader variant. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the ambient field (complex numbers), the degree restriction n > 1, the requirement involving every derivative P^(k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1, and the conclusion that P must be a pure power b(z−a)^n with b ≠ 0. It also stays within the paper’s main complex-polynomial version rather than drifting to the real or positive-characteristic side remarks. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that P is a univariate polynomial in C[z].
Unpack “shares a root with P^(k)” as: for each k = 1, 2, ..., n−1, there exists c_k ∈ C such that P(c_k) = P^(k)(c_k) = 0.
Clarify that the shared root c_k may depend on k; the paper explicitly warns that one should not assume a single common root works for all derivatives.
Specify that P^(k) denotes the ordinary kth derivative of P with respect to z.
Keep the scope exactly over C; the paper mentions characteristic-0 transfer and characteristic-p counterexamples only as nearby context, not as part of the conjecture itself.
Do not add extra hypotheses on the roots of P, such as all roots being real, all roots being distinct, or the same root being shared with every derivative.
refined_question: Let n > 1 be an integer, and let P(z) ∈ C[z] be a univariate polynomial of degree n. Assume that for every k = 1, 2, ..., n−1 there exists c_k ∈ C such that P(c_k) = P^(k)(c_k) = 0. Must there exist complex numbers a and b with b ≠ 0 such that P(z) = b(z−a)^n?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s exact formal statement. The introduction says Section 7 ends by stating the Casas-Alvero conjecture, and §7.3 presents it verbatim as Problem 30. The only paper-critical clarification your draft leaves implicit is that the common zero may vary with k; the sentence immediately after Problem 30 makes that explicit. The later remarks on the real-rooted version, characteristic-0 transfer, and characteristic-p counterexamples are neighboring context rather than equivalent reformulations, so the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should stay over C and keep the original derivative-sharing hypothesis unchanged. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
